summary: Tested the new video production flow on the backend and in the UI. Covered: required hours = weekly_hours x semester_weeks x 2/3, the full admin/teacher approval cycle (send, return, edit, send, recall, accept, issue, complete, reopen, terminate, plus wrong-state actions that should give 400), lump-sum item accrual including partial, payments (pending, confirm with VR receipt, dispute, balance cap, delete rules), contract and statement PDFs, studio-only money hiding, the per-teacher app visibility flag, letterheads, and the semester_weeks setting. Backend: 19 of 20 pytest pass. The one failure is a real money leak: PUT /settings sends default_items back to a studio-only user. A manual script also found an overpayment bug in disputed payments. Frontend: every requested data-testid flow works for admin and for a studio-only user, except the same settings leak, which shows in the UI after the studio user clicks save.

critical.issue: Money leak to studio-only users. The response is the full _settings(), including default_items with amounts, even when the caller has no finance permission (not _fin). Stored data is safe because default_items are preserved. But VpSettings.tsx calls setF(r.data) after saving, so a studio employee who clicks save then sees the section 'البنود الافتراضية للعقد الجديد' with all amounts. Fix: before returning, pop default_items when not _fin(u).

Overpayment through disputed payments. The cap uses balance = accrued - paid - pending, and disputed payments are left out. The teacher can still confirm a disputed payment later (allowed for status pending or disputed). Reproduced: accrued 50,000; payment P1 of 50,000 disputed; admin adds P2 of 50,000 (allowed); teacher confirms P2 and then P1, so paid = 100,000 and balance = -50,000. Fix: count disputed with pending in the cap (in _progress or add_payment), or stop confirming a disputed payment once it would exceed accrued.

minor.issue: An accepted item can be set back to pending or delivered after payments were received, so the balance goes negative (accrued 0, paid 100,000). There is no guard or warning.

These do not check app_visible. They use _my_tids, not _visible_tids, so a hidden teacher can still cancel or edit sessions and check availability. The brief says the teacher's my-endpoints should be denied when hidden.
A terminated contract goes straight back to issued (binding) with no teacher re-approval. Confirm this is intended.
'ملحق تعديل' changes item amounts or hours on a binding contract with no teacher re-approval and no change to the status flow. Confirm this is intended.

The backend has_permission reads user.permissions, but /auth/me uses role defaults plus custom_permissions and ignores user.permissions. A user created with permissions=['vp_studio'] gets API access but the UI says 'ليس لديك صلاحية'. With custom_permissions=['vp_studio'] both work. This existed before this change.

ui_bugs.issue: After clicking vp-set-save, the default items block with money amounts appears. This comes from the backend PUT /settings response.

action_items: In put_settings, strip default_items from the response when not _fin(u).
Include disputed payments in the cap (or block confirming a disputed payment past accrued) so paid can never exceed accrued.
Optional: block or warn on downgrading an accepted or partial item when received payments would go above the new accrued.
Optional: use _visible_tids in my_cancel, my_session_edit and availability so app_visible=false fully denies the teacher's my-endpoints.
critical_code_review_comments: put_settings returns money (default_items) to non-finance users. get_settings strips it, put_settings does not.
In _progress, disputed payments count as neither paid nor pending, which leaves the cap open to overpayment.

notify_users spreads extra at the top level, so extra.type overrides ntype ('video_production'). push_data reads extra['data'], which VP never sets, so FCM pushes carry no route data. This is a minor push deep-link issue.
Disputed payments show in the UI with the teacher note, but the admin can only delete them. There is no 'resend' or 'resolve' action.
